result.summary: Two Type E design artefacts produced for the two remaining code blockers (GH-366 and GH-374) surfaced by Step 3 verification of GitHub #364 / ISS-0106. (1) src/design/fix-ISS-0110.md specifies the narrow 90s/5s lock_timeout bracket around tests/integration/helpers.zig:99's pg_advisory_lock acquire inside runMigrations(), mirroring byte-for-byte the proven fc5884b / ISS-0107 Rework-1 pattern at line 487 (same values, same connection type, same plain-sequential-SET, NOT defer/errdefer/SET LOCAL). Source validation: helpers.zig:99 acquire, helpers.zig:487 acquire bracket, helpers.zig:516 begin. Evidence validation: scratch/WF03-gh364-20260801-step03-full-integration-utf8.log lines 70, 97, 124, 160, 187 (and 38 more) showing 44× 55P03 at line 99; zero 55P03 at line 487 (proving the proven Rework-1 pattern works at line 487 already). The design explicitly rejects blanket timeout inflation (citing the 'widening a critical section's scope without checking interaction with an existing timeout' anti-pattern in docs/anti-patterns.md, cross-referenced to GitHub #366), retries, sleeps, second lock keys, removal of the line-99 lock, global integration serialization, changes to build.zig, changes to test_iss503_rls_removal.zig, and changes to vendor/pg/pg.zig. Safety nets (ambient 5s lock_timeout everywhere else in the file + statement_timeout='60s' for the inner migration DDL walk) are explicitly preserved. (2) src/design/fix-ISS-0111.md specifies deterministic cross-platform Python interpreter resolution via a new file-local resolveTestPython helper at the top of tests/integration/tnt_schema_isolation_test.zig (after testDbUrl at line 30-50) using strict 3-step priority order: BPM_TEST_PYTHON env override → .venv interpreter (Scripts\python.exe on Windows, bin/python on POSIX) → bare 'python3' fallback. Helper returns a []const u8 with explicit ownership analysis for all three return paths (env-var slice from std.process.Environ, venv path dup, bare-literal dup); callers free via defer alloc.free(python) which fires LIFO after the std.process.run call. Error behavior: error.MissingTestPythonInterpreter with a clear stderr remediation message mirroring testDbUrl's MissingTestDatabaseUrl pattern. Both std.process.run callsites (lines 591-593 and 659-661) updated consistently. The design rejects hard-coded user-specific paths, disabling the tests, where.exe/which/registry consultation, AppExecutionAlias disabling, changing tools/lint_migration_schema.py, MSW / HTTP / subprocess mocking, and bundling a Python interpreter. Both designs preserve no-overlap with the already-approved #364 barrier (build.zig structure and test_iss503_rls_removal.zig doc comment are explicitly 'NOT touched'). Both designs pass tools/lint_design_artefact.py with BLOCKER=0, MAJOR=0 (only MINOR E030 noise on legitimate references to public.schema_migrations / public.events — the linter cannot distinguish canonical platform tables from business tables, a known over-flag cataloged for future DOC-UPDATER housekeeping). No source, build, test, migration, or frontend implementation file is modified by this step. Next: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 03d) for revalidation of both designs, then BACKEND-DEV (Step 03e) for implementation, then TEST-RUNNER (Step 03f) for fresh full-suite evidence covering both blockers together.

explicit_non_solutions: No sleep calls anywhere on the test path.
No retry-on-55P03 / deadlock-retry wrappers around the line-99 acquire.
No inflation of ambient lock_timeout='5s' set by configureSessionTimeouts().
No second lock key (would reopen the same two-key race ISS-0107's chosen_resolution explicitly rejected).
No removal of the line-99 advisory lock (would re-introduce the race ISS-0090 was filed to prevent).
No change to build.zig (the 55P03 errors are a function-internal timeout-scoping problem, not a scheduling/ordering problem).
No change to tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig (the #364 barrier doc comment is already correct; the 55P03 errors do not involve this file).
No change to vendor/pg/pg.zig (driver already correctly propagates PgError.ServerError).
No change to src/db/migrations.zig (migrator intentionally a 'dumb applier' with no locking or timeout configuration; that responsibility stays with the caller per the closed ISS-0107 investigation).
No disable of TC-TNT-02-03/04 (both are valid tests; the fix is to invoke them with the correct interpreter).
No hard-coded user-specific absolute Python path (env-dependent, brittle).
No disable of the Microsoft Store AppExecutionAlias (out-of-repo config change; cannot rely on this for CI).
No change to tools/lint_migration_schema.py (linter is correct; only the invocation needs the right interpreter).
No where.exe / which / py -3 / Windows registry consultation (would re-introduce the AppExecutionAlias ambiguity or add platform-specific code paths that the test cannot deterministically assert on).
No MSW / HTTP / subprocess mocking (test launches a real subprocess against the real linter; per docs/anti-patterns.md, mocking is forbidden in the test path).
No bundling a Python interpreter with the repo (out of scope; ~50MB of unrelated dependency).
No global integration serialization of all ~19+ test-integration binaries (over-reach; only specific acquire sites need bracketing).
